incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > SLO on cont-batch path (usw2) — auto-page to #eng-oncall at 2025-03-12T03:15:05Z :rotating_light:

alice_ng: seeing it too. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~650ms over last 10m, p99 up to ~4.2s. streaming stalls count x12.

ben_koh: logs show a bunch of "pack_wait" durations spiking, and pack sizes skewed: many tiny requests stuck behind a few huge seqlen requests.

carla_r: summary from metrics dump: 
```
metric: contbatch.p95_latency 650ms -> 700ms
metric: contbatch.p99_latency 4.2s -> 4.8s
metric: stream.stalls.count 18 -> 210 (10m)
metric: contbatch.avg_batch_size 14 -> 18
metric: contbatch.max_pending_seq_len 10240
```

carla_r: looks like mixed-seqlen amplification + scheduler fairness drift. KV cache churn higher than normal.

alice_ng: impact: a few high-throughput customers (ACME-PROD, beta-embed) saw increased tail and some timeouts. No wide customer 5xx spike yet but user-visible slow responses for streaming.

dave_sre: suggested quick mitigations we can toggle now:
- enable contbatch.preemptive_small_batches for us-west-2 (route small/short seqs to fast-path)
- temporarily cap max_batch_size=8 for cont-batcher on the affected fleet
- increase pack_timeout from 10ms -> 30ms to reduce packing jitter
- route heavy tenants to dedicated pool if available (route: tenant=ACME-PROD -> dedicated-usw2-1)

ben_koh: sharing commands I used in dev cluster, careful with flags:
```
opsctl feature-flag set contbatch.preemptive_small_batches true --env=prod --region=usw2
opsctl config update contbatch.max_batch_size=8 --selector fleet=contbatch-usw2
opsctl config update contbatch.pack_timeout_ms=30 --selector fleet=contbatch-usw2
```

alice_ng: applied preemptive flag to canary nodes (5%): p99 dropped from 4.8s -> 2.4s on canary within 90s. Streaming stalls decreased ~40% on canary.

carla_r: great. rolling to 30% now, watching KV eviction rate.

incident-bot: NOTE: paging escalation threshold hit — severity SLO breach window started. Please annotate customer impact.

eve_prod: ACME-PROD contacted support complaining about slow streaming (long gaps between tokens). They have non-critical production traffic but UX degraded. BetaCorp reported increased embedding latencies but no task failures.

dave_sre: immediate action plan:
1) finish enabling preemptive_small_batches across all contbatch-usw2 nodes (target 5m)
2) set max_batch_size=8 globally for contbatch-usw2 (target 10m rollback window)
3) create temporary routing rule for tenants with avg_seq_len>4096 -> dedicated-usw2-1
4) increase observability retention for contbatch metrics to capture full spike window
5) start postmortem doc and capture prompt sets causing long seqs (tag example requests)

ben_koh: note — lowering max_batch_size reduces throughput efficiency. we should monitor cost and latency tradeoff; plan to revert once pack scheduler fairness fix lands.

carla_r: digging into scheduler logs: found a bug where score decay for long-request priority wasn't applied after preemption; results in long seqs re-joining head-of-queue. I'll open an RFC/PR: scheduler:fix/preempt-reset-ttl.

alice_ng: for immediate customer relief, opsctl route rule applied for ACME-PROD -> dedicated-usw2-1. confirmation: routing took effect, they report lower p99 for 2 minutes.

alice_ng: also added a temporary alert: contbatch.p99_operational > 2s for 5m -> page SRE.

incident-bot: REMINDER: record the time window for SLO breach: start=2025-03-12T03:14:50Z, currently ongoing.

dave_sre: handoff note for next oncall: we disabled packing efficiency to prioritize latency (max_batch_size=8, preemptive enabled). KV churn is elevated; expect some cache warming. If p99 climbs after flag revert, escalate to eng-runtime.

carla_r: PR opened for scheduler TTL bug, link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/scheduler/pulls/948 (wip). Tests added.

eve_prod: customer comms: support notified ACME-PROD & BetaCorp that we're mitigating and routing their traffic; follow-up planned after postmortem.

ben_koh: logs to capture for postmortem: pack_wait hist, seq_len distribution, scheduler preemption counts, kv_hit_rate. snapshot commands:
```
metrics export contbatch.pack_wait.hist --since 15m > /tmp/pack_wait.json
query "select seq_len, count(*) from requests where region='usw2' group by seq_len" --out csv > /tmp/seqdist.csv
```

alice_ng: timeline so far:
- 03:14:50Z metric drift detected (p99 rise)
- 03:15:05Z incident-bot page -> this thread created
- 03:16:10Z enabled preemptive_small_batches canary -> p99 halved on canary
- 03:18:00Z roll to 30% -> global p99 trending down
- 03:20:30Z set max_batch_size=8 globally -> customer routing applied for top offenders

dave_sre: next steps for eng-runtime: patch scheduler TTL in PR, run small perf calibration with mixed seqlen traces, then revert packing knobs and enable fair rebalancer.

carla_r: assigning follow-ups: 
- carla_r: own postmortem (link placeholder)
- ben_koh: collect metrics snapshot + attach queries
- alice_ng: customer comms + timeline
- dave_sre: coordinate rollback plan with infra
dave_sre: OK handing off to night oncall @eve_prod at 03:25Z. If p99 rises above 2s after rollback, escalate to eng-runtime and page oncall@eng-runtime.

eve_prod: ack. Will watch p95/p99 and streaming stalls. If we see reversion, will reapply cap and notify.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE CREATED: incident-id=INC-20250312-0433, severity=page, owners=[carla_r, dave_sre], sla-breach=true.

alice_ng: final: collect a short set of example requests (anonymized) that triggered the path so runtime team can reproduce mixed-seqlen effect. I'll dump top 20 request sizes to S3 and attach to the doc. :white_check_mark:
